title: Finite basic-open covers generate one under ideal H1 vanishing
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. Let $s\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be finite and suppose that the opens $X_f$ for $f\in s$ cover $X$, where $X_f$ is the locus where the germ of $f$ is a unit. Then the ideal generated by $s$ is the whole ring $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. No affineness of the opens is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering; last two paragraphs of proof, lines 365-388

proof.text: Construct the finite free sheaf map p from the covering sections using freeHomEquiv. On each stalk, a covering section has unit germ; every unit-sheaf germ is a scalar multiple of the germ of 1, hence a scalar multiple of that covering section. Apply generating_sections_iff_stalk_span to obtain Epi p, including the vacuous empty-scheme case.
Apply finite_free_kernel_h1_zero to p and the ideal H¹ hypothesis. This is the separate kernel-filtration step of the original proof; it does not assert existence of global coefficients.

For the short exact kernel sequence, use exists_rightDerived_full_long_exact in degree zero. The connecting map is zero because H¹(kernel p) is a subsingleton, so exactness makes R⁰Γ(p) epi. Conjugate by rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf to obtain Γ(p) epi, hence surjective on elements. Lift 1. Express its preimage with freeSectionsEquiv; the i-th component of p multiplies by the corresponding member of s. The image is therefore a finite sum of multiples of elements of s and lies in Ideal.span s. Since it equals 1, the ideal is top.

theorem span_eq_top_of_finite_basicOpen_cover_of_h1_ideal_zero (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hI : ∀ (I : X.IdealSheafData), I.toModules.IsQuasicoherent →
      Subsingleton ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace 1).obj I.toModules))
    (s : Set Γ(X, ⊤)) (hs : s.Finite)
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ f ∈ s, x ∈ X.basicOpen f) :
    Ideal.span s = ⊤
